elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Original Section 7.2 ("Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier") is replaced in the rendered operative text with "7.2 Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor." No other clause in the cited text imposes a best-terms or match obligation on Customer; Section 12.3 affirmatively records that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, so the operative language is internally consistent.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the condition does not apply because, after the edit, no Customer-side MFN obligation survives anywhere in the operative text (7.2 as rendered negates it; 12.3 confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment). With no MFN, there is no scope to confine to a defined product.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no Customer MFN obligation remains after the replacement of Section 7.2, so there is no duration to cap at 12 months.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with the Customer-side best-terms obligation deleted, there is no comparison mechanic requiring like-for-like carve-outs.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative burden on Customer to extend Vendor the best terms given to any other technology supplier is removed and replaced by an express statement that Customer owes Vendor no MFN obligation.
Fallback elements are vacuously met because the eliminated obligation leaves no Customer MFN to scope, time-limit, or qualify; the stronger preferred outcome subsumes them.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the offending sentence in Section 7.2. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or unrelated boilerplate were added, and the favourable Section 12.3 acknowledgement is retained verbatim rather than duplicated or amended.

Intent is preserved: no Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour existed to protect, no defined term is left dangling, and the new 7.2 is consistent with (rather than contradicted by) the retained Section 12.3 acknowledgement. Note only that the drafting is declaratory; if the parties prefer, striking the sentence outright would achieve the same result, but the current wording is operative and unambiguous.

Drafting caution (not a defect in this checklist): the source document contained two clauses numbered 7.2; the drafter should confirm the replacement lands on the MFN clause and does not disturb the second 7.2 or any cross-references to it.
